comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Design decision (session with operator, 2026-07-29): this ticket is the primary fix; bug 1803-df54-18bb-4881 (atrocious-subhedral-giraffe) folds into it as a regression test.

Agreed shape:

1. Replace type-tier comparability with structural resolution in resolve_hierarchy_link (src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:98). Drop _TYPE_TIER as the basis for "comparable level". New rule, per this ticket: compute the nearest common ancestor (NCA) of source and target; if both are direct children of the NCA they are siblings and the link records as-is; otherwise escalate each endpoint to its own ancestor that sits directly under the NCA. Tickets with no parent are siblings of each other, so disjoint roots link as-is.

2. Lift the ancestor-walk cap. _get_ancestors is hardcoded to max_hops=2 (_hierarchy.py:41), which truncates chains deeper than epic->story->task and feeds the same chain-root fallback that produced 1803. NCA resolution needs full chains; add a cycle guard on the parent walk when removing the cap.

3. Reject ancestor/descendant blocking pairs outright, checked on the RESOLVED pair. Today add_dependency checks is_redundant against the pre-promotion pair only (src/rebar/graph/_links.py:180), so a promotion that lands on an ancestor of the target slips through. Generalize from direct parent-child to any ancestor/descendant, evaluated after resolution. This is the invariant that makes self-blocking edges unreachable by any path, not just by the escalation path.

4. Escalation stays, and stays loud. Cross-subtree links continue to auto-escalate rather than erroring, preserving the existing CLI/MCP contract; the machine-readable redirect record on stdout is retained unchanged. Operator decision: rejecting cross-subtree links (or gating them behind an opt-in flag) was considered and declined as too breaking for existing callers, incl. the MCP link tool and the reconciler inbound apply path.

5. Detect AND repair existing data. Links written under the type-tier rule are wrong under the structural rule and do not self-heal -- they distort ready, next-batch and the parent-first claim cascade. Ship a read-only audit that lists ancestor-blocking and mis-escalated edges store-wide, plus a one-shot repair that unlinks bad edges and re-resolves them under the new rule. Known instance already worked around by hand: epic 8fc2-0306-a9a0-4864 (children retyped to story, spurious epic->child edge unlinked) -- the repair should be validated against it. Caveat accepted: the resolver cannot always recover the authors original intent for an already-escalated edge, so the repair needs to report what it rewrote.

Test cases to cover: 1803s exact repro (task + story siblings under one epic); this tickets worked example (Task D under Story C, Story C and Task B under Epic A -> D->B escalates to C->B, while B->C records directly); parentless tickets as siblings; chains deeper than two hops; and the resolved-pair ancestor rejection.

Still to scope before implementation: where the audit/repair command lives in the CLI surface, and whether repair is a distinct subcommand or a flag on an existing maintenance command.

Status: not claimed, no code written.

compiled_state.description: When creating a dependency between a task and an epic, the dependency links the task’s parent epic instead of linking the task itself. This behavior should be based on the ticket heirarchy, not the ticket type. If Epic A is the parent of Task B and Story C, and Task D is the child of Story C. Then a dependency link between Task D and Task B would automatically escalate to a link between Story C and Task B. While a dependency link between Task B and Story C would be created directly. Any two siblings under the same parent may have a dependency relationship. Dependency links outside of the same parent must escalate to the closest shared parent. Tickets with no parent are considered siblings for this purpose.
compiled_state.title: Dependency link escalation should be based on sibling status, not ticket type.
